newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INRO rubber indicator hits intervention level.
newsitem.headline: INRO rubber indicator hits intervention level.

text.p: The International Natural Rubber Organisation's five-day indicator for rubber prices fell below 183 Malaysia/Singapore cents a kg on Friday, triggering the level for the group to buy rubber in the market.
The five-day indicator ended at 182.48 cents a kg on July 10, compared to 183.56 cents on July 9. At below 183 cents, INRO may buy rubber in the market.
An INRO official said on Friday the group could enter the market "anytime" to support rubber prices if they stayed at the current rate or slipped to the "must buy" level of 172 cents.
"As it is now, it's only at the may-buy level," said the official. He said INRO last intervened in the market in 1993.
Traders, however, doubted that the present level could attract an intervention from INRO.
"INRO will only intervene if it reaches around 177-180 cents...this will help the market," said a trader.

Rubber prices, in the doldrums for more than 18 months, have seen a particularly sharp fall in the last week owing to the flotation of the Thai baht, which dragged down prices of rubber in Thailand and elsewhere in the region.
The INRO's daily indicator was at 181.42 cents on July 10, against the 181.66 cents on July 9.
